title: Centered source masses give solution-uniform local potentials and Riesz tails

statement.quantifiers: n>=1,0<s<n,p,q>0; positive continuous everywhere-finite weighted Riesz integral solution.
statement.assertion: Origin forces A/B>-s; ball infima exclude pq<=1. Then positive scaling exponents yield int_BR f<=CR^(n-s-beta),g<=CR^(n-s-alpha), uniform int_B4(f+g+u+v) and exterior-ell potential<=C ell^(s-n).
assumptions: No solution-uniform global boundedness/decay or finite-energy assumption.

inputs: Exactly scoped integral/weak-PDE objects and source hypotheses.
outputs: Analytic lemma, proof mechanism or scope obstruction, not an external/formal certificate.
interface.precision: Exact order, dimension, origin/tail/local-versus-global conditions retained.
costs: Constants depend fixed equation parameters; numerical/effective values not supplied.

proof_mechanism: Coupled ball lower bounds control unit source masses.
Centered dilation transfers the same bound to every radius.
Positive alpha/beta sum dyadic tails; local kernel integrability and Tonelli give uniform local integrals.
obstructions: Local virial alone does not provide these uniform constants.
